content.text: {"title":"The Lantern That Learned to Whisper","premise":"After sunset in a small night garden, Mira and Sol want to give a welcome party for a shy visiting moth. Mira dreams of a bright, grand entrance; Sol wants the garden to feel quiet and safe; the moth wants to choose its own landing place. A lamp, a paper shadow-screen, a blue ribbon, and a bowl of moonflowers make the garden ready—but one choice can turn the welcome into a parade, a shadow show, or a gentle surprise.","cast_and_props":"Characters: Mira (child, wants a spectacular welcome; curiosity 2; knows lamp status, guest preference, and ribbon ownership as discovered), Sol (child, wants a calm welcome and believes the moth dislikes bright light until told otherwise), Luma (moth, wants to land near moonflowers and avoid direct glare; its preferences are represented by observed facts, not mind-reading). Props: lantern lamp, shadow-screen, blue ribbon, moonflower bowl, garden gate. State slots are declared for every entity: mira.memes.curiosity, mira.knows.lamp.lit, mira.knows.luma.preference, sol.memes.calm, sol.knows.lamp.lit, sol.knows.luma.preference, luma.preference, luma.location, lamp.lit, lamp.owner, screen.position, screen.owner, ribbon.owner, ribbon.tied, flowers.open, gate.open, welcome.mode, welcome.ready, welcome.guest_content, and each character's pivotal agreement or delight slot.","kernels_and_interactions":"Use five kernel families: observe/tell for discovering whether the lamp is lit and what Luma chooses; prepare for lighting the lantern, moving the screen, opening the gate, and arranging flowers; transfer for sharing the blue ribbon; negotiate for Mira and Sol choosing bright, shadow, or moonflower welcome modes; perform for the final welcome and Luma's landing. Inciting action: Mira opens the garden gate and calls, “Come see our welcome!” before either child knows where Luma will land. Problem A: Mira lights the lamp at full brightness and Luma hides behind the screen; the children must learn the lamp is too glaring, move the screen, and create a glowing shadow performance. Problem B: Sol ties the only blue ribbon to the gate, while Mira promises it to decorate Luma's landing flower; their conflicting wants produce a ribbon trade and a shared moonflower welcome. Problem C: Luma lands on the lamp before the children notice, and Mira mistakes the fluttering shadow for an invitation to perform; observation and telling reveal that Luma wants the moonflowers, changing the planned grand entrance into a quiet trail of flower lights. Reuse scenes such as look-at-lamp, tell-sol-about-luma, open-gate, arrange-flowers, and welcome-performance across all paths. Candidate IDs: open_gate, look_lamp, light_lamp, notice_luma_shadow, tell_sol_lamp, move_screen, offer_ribbon, transfer_ribbon, untie_ribbon, tie_flower, open_flowers, notice_luma, tell_mira_preference, dim_lamp, choose_shadow, choose_moonflower, perform_shadow, invite_luma, luma_lands, welcome_done. Use 18 candidates, 5–10 selected events. Mark only tell_sol_lamp and tell_mira_preference as pivotal. Rules may derive welcome.ready when gate.open, flowers.open, and welcome.mode is non-None; derive guest_content when luma.location is flowers or screen, but never infer knowledge automatically.","seed_parameters":"build(812196228) uses random.Random(seed). Seed-derived initial variants should choose one of three physical/social premises without a branch-number route: (1) lamp.lit=True, screen.position='behind_lamp', luma.location='screen', welcome.mode=None; (2) ribbon.owner='sol', ribbon.tied=True, flowers.open=False, welcome.mode=None; (3) luma.location='lamp', sol.knows.luma.preference=None, lamp.lit=True, welcome.mode='bright'. premise_keys: lamp.lit, luma.location, ribbon.owner, flowers.open. outcome_keys: welcome.mode, luma.location, welcome.guest_content. Initial values remain scalar booleans, strings, integers, or None. Conditions must guard physical access and knowledge: only Mira or Sol who has observed a fact may act on it; Luma's preference is learned through notice_luma or tell_mira_preference, never read directly in prose.","candidate_scenes":"Catalog every candidate with role beat or bridge. open_gate beat: Mira opens the gate and announces the welcome. look_lamp bridge: a child checks the lamp. light_lamp beat: Mira lights it brightly, making a sharp white pool. notice_luma_shadow beat: Sol discovers Luma hiding behind the screen and identifies the glare as the problem. tell_sol_lamp bridge: Mira tells Sol the lamp is lit. move_screen beat: Sol shifts the screen so the light makes moth-sized leaves. offer_ribbon bridge: Mira asks Sol for the blue ribbon. transfer_ribbon beat: Sol gives it up after agreeing to decorate the flowers instead of the gate. untie_ribbon bridge: Sol unties the gate ribbon. tie_flower beat: Mira ties the ribbon around the moonflower bowl. open_flowers beat: Sol opens the moonflowers and makes a soft landing path. notice_luma beat: Sol sees Luma choosing the moonflowers, discovering its preference. tell_mira_preference beat: Sol tells Mira where Luma wants to land. dim_lamp beat: Mira lowers the lamp so the flowers glow instead of glare. choose_shadow beat: the children agree on a shadow welcome. choose_moonflower beat: the children agree on a flower welcome. perform_shadow beat: leaves and wings dance across the screen. invite_luma bridge: Sol offers the moonflower path. luma_lands beat: Luma lands at the chosen place. welcome_done beat: the selected welcome becomes the final social accomplishment. Opening catalog needs at least two variants: one playful full-moon introduction and one hushed lantern introduction, each conditional on the initial premise. Scene cards should have two voice variants for major beats and concise bridge cards. Endings: bright-to-shadow ending when welcome.mode='shadow' and luma.location='screen'; ribbon-and-flower ending when welcome.mode='moonflower' and luma.location='flowers'; surprise-lamp ending when luma.location='lamp' and welcome.guest_content='unexpected'; each needs two 35–70-word variants and a final image rather than explanation. Lexicon phrases: lamp.lit=True -> 'was shining'; lamp.lit=False -> 'was dark'; luma.location='screen' -> 'the leafy screen'; luma.location='flowers' -> 'the moonflowers'; luma.location='lamp' -> 'the warm lamp rim'; welcome.mode='shadow' -> 'a shadow welcome'; welcome.mode='moonflower' -> 'a moonflower welcome'; ribbon.tied=True -> 'was curled around the gate'; ribbon.tied=False -> 'waited in Sol’s hand'.","constraints":"Implement import random and runtime only. Return WorldSpec with entities, initial, 18 immutable candidates, rules, labels, goal, premise_keys, outcome_keys, and prune=True. Declare every state slot before use; all keys begin with an existing entity ID. Use scene keyword arguments only, with atomic set_values, increments, and copies. Use observe, tell, and transfer at least once. Avoid abstract counters, branch numbers, mind-reading, automatic belief updates, and claims that Luma understands plans it has not observed. The goal should accept several outcomes, such as welcome.ready=True and welcome.guest_content=True, while outcome_keys preserve their different meanings. Require 5–10 selected events, reuse at least two scenes on materially different paths, and keep the prose between 220 and 400 words. No prose should say that a character knows a fact before an observe or tell event. No unused prop should appear in an ending. The final images are: moth-wings making leaf shadows, blue ribbon trembling around moonflowers, or Luma resting on the lamp rim while the children whisper beneath it.","different_endings":"1. Shadow Lantern: The screen fills with enormous leaf-shadows, then two tiny wings cross them. Mira’s grand glare has become a gentle theater, and Luma settles behind the moving leaves. 2. Blue Moonflower Welcome: The ribbon circles the flower bowl, not the gate. Luma lands in its blue loop, while Sol and Mira hold their breath and watch the petals nod. 3. Unexpected Lamp Guest: Luma remains on the warm lamp rim, turning the children’s planned welcome into a tiny golden audience. The children sit below, performing softly for the moth that chose its own front-row seat."}
